fields.description: Issue includes editorials and reports on alleged "Crime Commission" publicity tactics and federal anti-gambling investigations; an account and critique of the Miami Herald warehouse fire and fire-safety practices; coverage of Miami city election maneuvering around a newly required anti-Communist oath; discussion urging Black voter registration and commentary on race relations and municipal court cases; articles on press ethics including claims of press-bribery tied to the American Medical Association and Newspaper Week; church opposition to gambling and racetracks; and a statistical report on Miami International Airport passenger, cargo, and mail traffic for the first half of 1949.
